Physics Major, PhD
The PhD in physics prepares students for professional careers in government, industry or academic institutions. Students learn to perform independent research in thriving areas of physics. Original research is required and the PhD dissertation must be rigorously orally defended.
Campus Code
Knoxville Campus
UTSI Campus
Admissions Standards/Procedures
A student who enrolls in graduate study with the intention of attaining an advanced degree in physics will have completed an undergraduate major in physics or its equivalent.
These courses constitute the minimum courses prerequisite to graduate study.
PHYS 311-312, 321, 361 (See undergraduate catalog for more information on 300-level courses)
PHYS 431-PHYS 432, PHYS 421, PHYS 461, PHYS 411-PHYS 412 (See undergraduate catalog for more information on 400-level courses)
A student who intends to present physics as a graduate minor will have completed an undergraduate minor in physics or its equivalent.
Physics 311 and PHYS 431-PHYS 432 constitute the minimum course work prerequisite to a minor in physics.
The Graduate Record Examination (general and subject) are optional.
Academic Standards
Students should have at least a 3.00 GPA on the graduate core curriculum in physics.
Credit Hours Required
72 graduate credit hours beyond the bachelor’s degree
48 graduate credit hours beyond the master’s degree
Required Courses
All students are expected to take the graduate core curriculum in physics consisting of:
PHYS 521 - Quantum Mechanics
PHYS 522 - Quantum Mechanics
PHYS 531 - Classical Mechanics
PHYS 541 - Electromagnetic Theory
PHYS 551 - Statistical Mechanics
PHYS 571 - Mathematical Methods in Physics I
A minimum of 12 hours of 600-level courses with 3 additional hours at the 500 level or above with approval of the student’s Doctoral Committee
PHYS 600 - Doctoral Research and Dissertation (minimum 24 credit hours)
Non-Course Requirements
All first-year graduate students are required to take a diagnostic examination testing undergraduate physics during the fall semester registration period.
Students are required to find a research advisor and form a doctoral committee before the end of the second year of study. This committee is responsible for advising the student and monitoring their progress toward the doctoral degree.
Students must successfully pass a written qualifying examination testing their mastery of the graduate 500-level physics core courses usually taken in the first year. Students have two attempts to qualify with the timeline tied to their successful completion of the core graduate curriculum.
Students are required to complete a comprehensive examination before the end of their third year, which consist of a written research proposal based on current and proposed research and an oral defense of the proposal.
Students are required to write a doctoral dissertation describing an original and substantial (as determined by their thesis committee) contribution to research and complete a final oral examination in which the dissertation is defended.
